resources.string: The entrance to a quiet museum lined with unusual exhibits.
Museum visit complete. Every exhibit may be revisited.
All exhibit progress and attempts will be cleared, and you will return to the museum entrance.
A six-panel museum illustration showing a pen vanishing from papers and reappearing on a filing cabinet.
A dim museum room with a scrambled clock, altered book titles, a fractured globe, and a tabletop model of the solar system.
Study the illustration and choose the detail that best answers each clue.
Which detail remembers numbers in the wrong order?
Which detail remembers familiar names incompletely?
Which detail remembers places as broken pieces?
That detail is strange, but it does not fit this clue. Look again.
That memory fits. One detail becomes clearer.
The almost-familiar room comes into focus. You found every altered memory.
All three altered memories have been identified.
A dense museum display where paperwork moves from an inbox through organizing, planning, and rearranging before returning to the inbox.
Trace the paper trail in order, beginning where new tasks enter the display.
The trail returns to the inbox. Choose an action that will break the loop.
The paperwork looks busy, but nothing leaves the room.
The paper trail advances. Keep following the arrows.
That is not where this paper goes next. Follow the arrows from the last traced step.
The same task has returned to the inbox. The activity is a loop.
You have already traced the full loop. Choose how to interrupt it.
Trace the full paper loop before trying to interrupt it.
That creates more activity, but the task remains unfinished.
One task is complete. The loop stops when work produces an outcome.
You broke the loop in %1$d choices.
A dark museum workshop filled with meetings, code, workflow diagrams, planning boards, and metrics that track activity, output, and undefined impact.
Classify each piece of evidence by what it actually proves.
Activity is effort. Output is something produced. Impact is a changed outcome.
The team held twelve alignment meetings this month.
A revised workflow guide is now available to the team.
New users complete setup thirty percent faster.
The team spent forty hours reviewing code.
Three automation scripts are now available to the team.
Busy signals can look alike. Decide whether this is effort, a deliverable, or a changed result.
Correct. This records effort expended, not something produced or changed.
Correct. This is a deliverable, but its effect is not yet known.
Correct. This describes an outcome that changed.
Look again: this only records work being performed.
Look again: this names something produced, not what it changed.
Look again: this reports a changed outcome, not merely work or a deliverable.
The dashboard clears. Activity and output support progress, but impact proves that something changed.
A dim museum room of suspended moments, including a tilted cup poised above a still-dry table, an unfinished apple, and an open book hovering near a chair.
Move the moment forward, then preserve it exactly before consequence.
The room is settled. Watch for the instant when possibility becomes imminent.
The cup edges toward the table’s rim.
The cup has tipped, but the table is still dry.
Nothing is close enough to becoming.
The spill happened. The room quietly resets the moment.
The moment is preserved exactly before consequence.
You preserved the moment in %1$d choices.
Inspect the scene. The pen may return somewhere you have already checked.
No pen here. Remember this spot.
Still empty. Try a different part of the scene.
Something shifted somewhere you already checked.
No pen here. It did not move.
The pen is back! You found the anomaly.
The pen has reappeared in a previously checked location.
This exhibit is locked. Complete the previous exhibit first.
You solved the exhibit in %1$d inspections.
